- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.5) and model forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If recent events show high supply net (positive) and true price spikes, model may be underestimating downside risk — adjust downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast decline rate to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) and model is flat or rising, force downward adjustment to reflect pessimism.  
- If event net is negative (supply/supply imbalance) and true price falls sharply, model may be lagging — adjust early for downward momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true price deviates >10% from forecast, check sentiment alignment — if sentiment contradicts price movement, reverse bias direction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes followed by sharp drops, model should anticipate mean reversion — add downward bias after peak.  
- When supply net is high and sentiment is neutral, model should not ignore event impact — apply conservative downward adjustment.
